neighbours.label: a clause-linking conjunction (' because', ' since', ' or', ' but') that continues an affirmative clause mid-sentence; the opposite side of the + pole's 'but/so after a clause stating absence'
fire: The bridge was closed for repairs last week because the steel cables had started to rust.
Engineers chose this design for the turbine since it handles high winds very well.
The leaves can be burned in a small pile or composted in a bin behind the shed.
The theory was dismissed for decades but has recently gained support among biologists.
These valleys are important to geologists because they expose very old rock layers.
The sample must be cooled quickly or it will react with oxygen in the air.
We will discuss the sensor array in more detail later since it is the key part of the setup.
Farmers rotate their crops every season because it keeps the soil rich in nitrogen.
quiet: The bridge was closed for repairs last week. The steel cables had started to rust.
Engineers chose this design for the turbine. It handles high winds very well.
The leaves can be burned in a small pile in the yard behind the shed.
The theory was dismissed for decades. Biologists have recently looked at it again.
These valleys are important to geologists. They expose very old rock layers.
The sample must be cooled quickly. Oxygen in the air reacts with it.
We will discuss the sensor array in more detail later in the next chapter.
Farmers rotate their crops every season to keep the soil rich in nitrogen.

notes: Card: ' because' x7, ' or' x3, ' but' x2, ' since' in expository prose, after an affirmative clause. The + pole (held) is ', but/so' after a negated clause and code 'else'.
